items_missed: Third floor at BOTH origin and destination — Alyssa volunteered it unprompted, along with 'washers and dryers, and things like that, so it'll be pretty heavy stuff'. Zachary's entire response was 'Yes ma'am, all encompassing.' He never asked about an elevator, never asked how many flights, and never adjusted the eight-hour estimate. Three flights of stairs at both ends with an appliance is not a standard one-bedroom load.
No elevator question at all, on a third-floor-to-third-floor move.
Home size never verified — he read 'one bedroom apartment' off the quote form and estimated against it, but never confirmed it with the caller, who is quoting on behalf of a friend and may not know.
Move date never asked. He priced against a Thursday pulled from the form while the caller was openly telling him 'I don't know if she's going to be moving next month or not'.
Packing service never offered or priced — a long-haul move where load quality directly drives the drive-day clock.
No probe on boxes, storage, additional stops, additional rooms, long walks, narrow access, or parking.
No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' — went straight from name capture into a $1,056 travel fee.

Clock speech almost entirely absent: no 'clock starts on site when the contract opens', no 2.5-hour minimum, no fifteen-minute increments. Only 'as long or as little as you need the crew for' carried any of it.
Number of movers never stated. The $2,758 total is built on two movers at $97 for eight hours plus $1,206 in fees, but the customer has no way to derive crew size from anything he said.

Zero differentiators: No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, and the full no-hidden-fees pitch were all absent — on a call whose headline number is $2,758. Nothing was offered to justify the price.
'Pricing is super simple' opener missing; what's-included never enumerated; disassembly/reassembly never mentioned.
Save Your Ass speech entirely absent — and on a long-distance move billed hourly with a driving leg, prep advice is worth more here than on any local job.
No booking attempt and no attempt to pin down a date range. He never asked when the friend is targeting, so there was no availability conversation to have.
No deposit required never mentioned — one of Einstein's strongest differentiators, and the obvious counterweight to a $2,758 quote.
'Any other questions before I let you go?' never asked; hours of operation never given.
Insurance never explained — no No Worries, no 60c/lb baseline — despite appliances and three flights of stairs in play.
Used the customer's name only twice ('basically, Alyssa' and 'you don't have to do that Alyssa') — short of the 3+ bar.
top_strength: The email handoff was the best-executed moment on this call and genuinely customer-first. The instant he heard Alyssa say 'sorry, I'm trying to write all this down', he stopped her: 'you don't have to do that Alyssa, if you give me about five minutes I can type all this up in an email.' He then explained that the email carries his notes so that if she calls back and doesn't get him, anyone can look it up by name or email and she won't have to fill the form out again — that removes real friction for a caller quoting on someone else's behalf. He also confirmed her email spelling character by character. His day-of-week rate tiering was clear and complete ($97 Monday-Thursday, $103 Friday-Saturday, Sunday in between) with an honest reason for it, and he handled the quote-expiration question well: the quote does not expire, only the date-driven hourly rate changes.
coaching_note: Zachary, this call was efficient and clear but it gave the customer a $2,758 number with nothing attached to it, and that is why it scores where it does. Highest-leverage fix: when Alyssa told you it was third floor at both ends with a washer and dryer, you answered 'yes ma'am, all encompassing' and kept the eight-hour estimate. That is an estimate-accuracy problem, not just a scorecard problem. It should have been: 'Good to know — three flights on both ends with an appliance will add time. Is there an elevator at either building? Let me build that in, because I'd rather quote you honestly now than surprise your friend on move day.' Stairs and appliances are the two variables most likely to blow an eight-hour estimate. Second priority: you quoted a big number and defended none of it. Before the price, or immediately after, run the differentiators — 'That includes gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap, pads, and tools, plus our No Worries Damage Coverage up to $2,000, our On-Time Guarantee, and we don't take a deposit to hold the date.' Third: you never asked when the friend is moving. One question — 'when is she targeting?' — turns this from a price quote into a booking conversation, and lets you offer a Monday-through-Thursday date and save her real money. Add the prep speech too: on a long-haul hourly move, telling her that boxed and consolidated equals a shorter clock is the single easiest way to make that price feel manageable.
phone_presence_notes: Clear, organized, and the 'don't write it down, I'll email it' catch showed real attentiveness, but the call was transactional overall — no empathy marker for a $2,758 quote, no rapport built, and only two uses of her name.
